compiled:
📰 General

Veteran Airline Stowaway Appears Again, Disrupting Newark-to-Milan Flight •

Svetlana Dali, a repeat stowaway offender, was apprehended on a flight from Newark to Milan on Wednesday. This incident occurred more than a year after she previously stowed away on a New York-to-Paris flight. Authorities took Dali into custody following the disruption to the flight’s schedule. Investigations are ongoing to determine how she accessed the aircraft.

🌍 World

Jimmy Lai’s Fraud Conviction Overturned: A Significant Victory for Hong Kong Activists •

An appellate court in Hong Kong has overturned the fraud convictions against Jimmy Lai, a former media tycoon and prominent pro-democracy activist. The ruling represents a rare success for Lai, who has been embroiled in numerous legal challenges since his criticism of Beijing. The court’s decision stemmed from concerns about the handling of evidence during Lai’s trial. Lai, 78, remains a key figure in Hong Kong’s pro-democracy movement despite ongoing legal pressures.

🦅 US

Berlin Film Festival Faces Crisis as Director Ousted Amidst Political Pressure •

The Berlin International Film Festival is grappling with a significant crisis following the removal of its director, Tricia Tuttle. The decision, reportedly driven by political pressure surrounding the festival’s stance on the Israel-Gaza conflict, has raised concerns about the future of the event. Unlike other prominent film festivals, Berlin’s location as a national capital has made it a focal point for political demonstrations and criticism. This situation presents a unique challenge for the festival, potentially impacting its ability to operate effectively. The removal of Tuttle underscores the increasing difficulty for cultural institutions to navigate complex geopolitical issues.

💰 Business

Washington Post Suffers Massive $100 Million Loss, Triggering Layoffs •

The Washington Post reported a loss exceeding $100 million in 2023, a significant financial downturn that prompted a substantial restructuring. As a result of the losses, the newspaper implemented layoffs, eliminating approximately one-third of its workforce. Company leaders attributed the shortfall to declining print advertising revenue and challenges in transitioning to digital subscriptions. The layoffs represent a major shift in the Post’s operational structure following years of financial difficulties.

💻 Technology

Resident Evil Requiem on Switch 2 Achieves Impressive Frame Rates with DLSS •

Digital Foundry’s analysis reveals that Capcom utilized Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS) to deliver playable frame rates across the Nintendo Switch 2 version of Resident Evil Requiem. The game consistently achieved 60 frames per second in most areas, demonstrating effective optimization. Resolution varied depending on the scene, typically targeting 720p, though some areas utilized lower resolutions. Capcom’s implementation of DLSS proved crucial in maximizing performance on the handheld console.

🎭 Entertainment

Jonathan Majors Lands New Action Role with The Daily Wire Following Legal Troubles •

Following his guilty verdict on domestic violence charges, actor Jonathan Majors is returning to film projects with support from The Daily Wire. He is currently filming an action movie in South Carolina, details of which remain undisclosed. This marks a significant shift in Majors’ career trajectory after his involvement with Marvel Studios. The project represents a new partnership for the actor with the conservative media company.

🏅 Sports

Netflix Scores First Live F1 Race Broadcast in the United States •

Netflix has secured the rights to broadcast its inaugural live Formula 1 race to US audiences through a partnership with Apple TV. This marks a significant shift in F1’s broadcasting landscape, as Apple TV now holds the exclusive US television rights. The agreement allows Apple TV+ subscribers to watch the Canadian Grand Prix live. Previously, F1’s US rights were held by ESPN, highlighting a major change in the sport’s distribution strategy.

🔬 Science

ULA Vulcan Rocket Anomaly Delays Pentagon’s 2026 Launch Timeline Significantly •

A recent anomaly during ULA’s Vulcan Centaur rocket launch resulted in an unexpected debris plume from one of the boosters. The mission successfully deployed two national security satellites into orbit, but the subsequent investigation revealed a critical issue with the booster’s engine. This discovery has prompted a thorough review of the Vulcan Centaur’s performance and capabilities. Consequently, the U.S. Space Force has revised its 2026 launch schedule, pushing back several planned missions. Further analysis is underway to determine the full extent of the impact on future operations.

🩺 Health

Microplastics Found in Prostate Tumors, Raising New Health Concerns •

Researchers at NYU Langone Health discovered microplastic particles within the tissue of nine out of ten prostate tumors analyzed. The study identified concentrations of microplastics approximately 2.5 times higher than previously reported in human tissue. Scientists believe the microplastics may have entered the body through everyday exposure to plastic products. Further research is underway to investigate the potential impact of these particles on tumor growth and patient outcomes.
